title: stackfoundry product profile (.stackfoundry/product.json)
description: What kind of product this repo is, inferred by the surveyor and confirmed at init, owned by the team. whats-next reads it to choose the domain to research and to weigh its suggestions. Checked with `stackfoundry product check`.

summary.description: What it does and for whom, in one or two sentences.

category.description: The kind of product in plain words, specific enough to research: "B2C online store for physical goods", "developer CLI for database migrations", "internal staff scheduling tool".

domainId.description: Kebab id of the domain brief, .stackfoundry/domain/<domainId>.json. Products of the same kind share an id.

audiences.description: Who uses it: consumers, businesses, staff, developers, other services.

channels.description: Where it is used: web, mobile, desktop, API, CLI, in person.

markets.description: Countries or regions it serves; they decide which regulations the domain research covers.

monetization.description: How it makes money, or 'none' (open source, internal).

stage.description: Where it is in its life: an MVP needs table stakes first, a mature product differentiators and debt reduction.

goals.description: What the team wants next, in its own words.

nonGoals.description: What the team decided not to do; whats-next never recommends these.

evidence.description: Why the category was inferred: each claim with the repo path that shows it.
